items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: But the players that were my contemporaries that are still active are Dick Wellstead on piano, who was from Greenwich, Connecticut, and Johnny Glazel, who played trumpet from Scarsdale, and Charlie Traeger was a bass player from Greenwich.

ctx.x: That group has been written up, I know at times, in the old magazines and all and other wives. Can you tell some of the other fellows that you played with when you started?

Yeah. Well, there was an earlier group that were older than I who have not kept up their professional activities. But the players that were my contemporaries that are still active are Dick Wellstead on piano, who was from Greenwich, Connecticut, and Johnny Glazel, who played trumpet from Scarsdale, and Charlie Traeger was a bass player from Greenwich. He's still playing. Let me see. Jerry Blumberg came in on the scene later. He was from Baltimore.
Jerry was here two weeks ago. He didn't see him.
